Hi Sumit — really glad the demo landed. Attached is a first-pass MAP and an acceptance-tests markdown. High-level summary below so procurement/risk have something to review quickly.

Mutual Action Plan (summary):
- Week 0 (kickoff): access + data onboarding checklist; legal & security intake complete.
- Week 1-2 (integration): test harness + sample traffic; initial smoke tests.
- Week 3 (validation): acceptance tests run against your validation prompt set; concordance and latency measured.
- Week 4 (close/decision): go/no-go signoff or remediation sprint.

Key acceptance tests (pass/fail):
- Latency: 95th percentile token generation <= 350ms on reserved Dedicated nodes under your expected QPS (specified in MAP_v1.xlsx).
- Concordance: end-to-end task accuracy >= 90% measured on your 250-sample validation set (we'll run seeded runs and share traces).
- Safety/regressions: no P0 safety hits on instrumentation and at most 1.5% drop in NPS-like signal from baseline.

Exit gates (what triggers stop):
- Any sustained 95th percentile latency breach > 400ms for 6 consecutive hours.
- Concordance dropping below 85% on two consecutive daily runs.
- Critical security finding from your Risk team that requires platform isolation.

Responsibilities: Redwood: provide test harness, run quantized baseline, and share token-level latency breakdowns. CareStack: maintain validation prompt canonical set, run user-acceptance sampling, and approve signoff.

I've attached: MAP_v1.xlsx (mutual timeline + owners), acceptance_tests.md (test definitions + sampling procedures), and a pilot-sla-draft.pdf for procurement to review.

Next steps: if this looks good, can we lock a kickoff for Monday 2026-04-26?

—Neha
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Adding technical guardrails and confirmation of measurement methods so there's no ambiguity for signoff. A few clarifications:

1) Latency measurement: we'll report token-level p50/p95/p99 from the Redwood agent inside your VPC (or dedicated pool) and correlate with e2e times measured at your app layer. For contract purposes we use the agent-side p95.
2) Concordance measurement: we'll seed the runs (deterministic RNG) and run three independent trials; the canonical metric is the majority-vote match rate vs your labeled expected outputs. We log all outputs for audit.

Technical fail-safe plan (short):
- Canary routing: 10% -> 100% ramp with automatic rollback if any exit gate trips during ramp.
- Immediate fallback: auto-route to a smaller model with same interface + degrade tolerably for latency-sensitive endpoints.
- Evidence: trace artifacts + delta report (tokens, latencies, model version).

I'll be available on the kickoff. Can we include a short security sync (30m) day-of to validate audit log delivery and retention controls?

—Karthik
